newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says Iran releases some POWs.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says Iran releases some POWs.

text.p: Iraq said on Saturday that its former foe Iran had freed 722 Iraqi prisoners of war jailed since their 1980-1988 war.
But the official Iraqi News Agency (INA), quoting a statement by Iraq's Foreign Ministry, said Baghdad wanted Iran to account for all Iraqi POWs.

"The Iraqi government, while it looks positively to freeing this limited number of Iraqi prisoners of war and highly appreciates the Iranian initiative, hopes Iran would free all Iraqi prisoners of war," INA quoted the statement as saying.
Baghdad had said in the past that Iran was still holding 20,000 Iraqi POWs.
Iraq and Iran signed an agreement last year on mutual relations and the issue of POWs and remains of soldiers killed during the war, but did not announce the details.

Both have exchanged several hundred POWs and remains of soldiers. In October, Tehran freed 150 Iraqi POWs and in August the remains of 400 Iraqis and 65 Iranians were delivered to army officials from the two countries.
Accounting for soldiers missing in action and POWs is among the thorniest issues hindering efforts to improve relations.
